_comment: Copy to ~/.claude/settings.local.json and edit. installer/install.sh merges this on top of config/settings.json and RENDERS the result to ~/.claude/settings.json — Claude Code itself never reads this file (its only user-scope source is ~/.claude/settings.json; `claude --setting-sources`'s 'local' means the *project's* .claude/settings.local.json). So edits here take effect on the next install.sh run, not instantly. Set a plugin to false to disable a common one on this machine; add new ones to enable per-machine extras. The model/effortLevel/tui/theme keys below are per-machine preferences kept OUT of the synced common file — override each as this machine needs. Do NOT add alwaysThinkingEnabled here: it is pinned true in the synced config/settings.json (0ece959) because effortLevel xhigh is only legal while thinking is on, and setting it false on a machine whose effortLevel is xhigh makes every request 400. Anything the CLI writes into the rendered file (/model, /config, `claude plugin enable -s user`) is captured back into this file by the next install.sh run, so preferences are not lost.
_shadowing_warning: Claude Code honours exactly ONE settings.local.json — the NEAREST one. Inside a project that has its own .claude/settings.local.json with an enabledPlugins map, that map fully REPLACES this file's map (no per-key merge), so plugins enabled ONLY here are silently disabled in that project — no error, and `install.sh`/plugin_sync still report green (they only warn). Entries in config/settings.json are immune: they always merge in. So for a plugin you want everywhere, either add it to the lab-wide config/settings.json, or re-declare it in each project's own settings.local.json. Always confirm with `claude plugin list` run FROM the project directory, never from $HOME. Verified 2026-07-27.
_optional_plugins_note: Opt-in personal plugins (NOT enabled lab-wide — absent from config/settings.json, marketplaces not in extraKnownMarketplaces): remotion@remotion, ui-ux-pro-max@ui-ux-pro-max-skill, marketing-skills@marketingskills, claude-mem@thedotmack (marketplace name is 'thedotmack', not 'claude-mem'). Enable by running /sync-claudebase (step 4k detects, asks per plugin, then registers the marketplace + installs at user scope), or manually: `claude plugin marketplace add <ref> && claude plugin install <name> -s user`. List each one you enable here (e.g. "remotion@remotion": true) — that is what re-enables it on the next render, and what keeps future syncs from flagging it as reverse drift. But listing it here is NOT enough to make it active inside a project that ships its own enabledPlugins map — see _shadowing_warning. Verify with `claude plugin list` that Status reads 'enabled', not merely installed. claude-mem adds session-start injection and needs the `bun` runtime — see docs/ai-usage-fitting.md before keeping it.
_headroom_note: headroom (opt-in token-compression proxy) is NOT installed or updated by install.sh — /sync-claudebase step 4j detects it and asks. It routes claude through a local proxy to cut input tokens. Two ways to route, pick one per machine: (a) you type `claude` yourself -> run `headroom wrap claude` instead; nothing goes in this file and nothing persists, easiest to undo. (b) something else spawns claude (container entrypoint, harness, daemon) -> there is no wrap point, so add an env block to this file: "env": { "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:8787" }, then re-run installer/install.sh so it renders into ~/.claude/settings.json. Only add it if `headroom proxy` actually runs on this machine — a URL pointing at a dead localhost:8787 breaks every claude call. Never put it in config/settings.json: that file is synced, so the proxy URL would ship to every machine and break the ones with no proxy running. Check with `headroom doctor` — its claude row reads the rendered ~/.claude/settings.json, not this file, so it only turns green after an install.sh run. COST, weigh it before picking either route: routing at all disables Remote Control (/rc) and the 1M context window, because Claude Code gates both on the base URL client-side (upstream #746/#1158) — this hits `headroom wrap claude` too, which sets the same variable for its child. Compression and RC+1M are mutually exclusive. On a machine you drive remotely, or one running a 1M-context model, leave this unset and wrap only the sessions that want compression. PORT: give every machine its own port from the 18787+ block and record it here. There is no central allocation list — the port is per-machine state, so pick any free number in the block and settle ownership with the lsof check below, which catches a forward that a stale list would have called free. Never the default 8787 on two machines: VS Code Remote-SSH forwards a remote port to the SAME local port, so a local deployment bound there cannot bind and keepalive-respawns forever (exit 3) while `headroom install status` still says healthy (the forward answers the probe — confirm with `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN` that a Python process owns the socket). Always bind 127.0.0.1, never 0.0.0.0 — on a flat overlay network (Tailscale, WireGuard, ZeroTier) that publishes an unauthenticated credential-forwarding proxy to every node — and always point ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at this machine's own loopback, never another host's address. `headroom install apply --preset persistent-service` makes the proxy survive reboot; with the env route active, `headroom wrap` is redundant.
